- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is negative or volatile (e.g., post-80+ peaks, model jumps to 85+ while true settles lower).
- Underestimate downward trends when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -0.67 to -0.70) — model often fails to recognize bearish momentum.
- Overshoot early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mildly negative (e.g., -0.13 to -0.30) — model overreacts to short-term noise.
- Mean-reversion bias: model tends to overcorrect after sharp rallies (e.g., 82+ → 80+), but fails to recognize true long-term trend if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- Lagged response to sentiment: model reacts to sentiment shifts 2–3 days too late — especially when sentiment turns negative mid-period.
- Avoid extrapolating recent volatility into 30-day forecast — sentiment history shows diminishing impact after 5–7 days of strong sentiment.
- When sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, reduce forecast slope — model often overestimates recovery speed.
- Don’t assume sentiment is linear — model often treats sentiment as a static multiplier, ignoring its decay or reversal patterns.
